text:
I HYPOTHESISED WE MIGHT HAVE NO ONE-SENTENCE ACCOUNT OF THIS LIBRARY. I CHECKED. WE HAVE ONE, IT IS GOOD, AND IT IS IN README LINE 6.

  "storymodel4s is a Scala 3 library for representing written stories, human recall of those
   stories, and the mapping between the two"

Twenty words. It names what it operates on, what it produces, and it would let a cognitive scientist decide relevance immediately. It passes the sixty-second test on its own.

AND THEN THE VERY NEXT CLAUSE BURIES IT:

  "— including the Autobiographical Interview, treated as recall against a *latent* source. It is
   neurosymbolic by construction: typed propositional structure (an AMR-compatible local kernel), a
   multiplex narrative graph with contexts, hierarchy, and typed temporal/causal relations, and
   embedding feature views that retrieve but never adjudicate."

Forty-four words, six pieces of vocabulary a first-time reader does not have -- neurosymbolic, AMR-compatible local kernel, multiplex narrative graph, latent source, feature views, adjudicate. A reader who was oriented by word twenty is lost by word forty.

SO THE PROBLEM IS NOT THAT WE CANNOT SAY WHAT THIS DOES. IT IS THAT WE SAY IT AND THEN IMMEDIATELY TALK OVER OURSELVES. That is a different defect from the one I diagnosed two hours ago and it changes the fix.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE DOCS SITE, and it makes the job smaller: the landing page does not need new prose invented, it needs the sentence WE ALREADY WROTE, standing alone, followed by the story example, with the neurosymbolic paragraph moved to wherever a reader who has decided to stay will meet it. My draft opened with the story and reached the same place; leading with README's own sentence and then the story is better, because it is already agreed language and it was already reviewed.

MY EARLIER HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND I WOULD RATHER SAY SO THAN LET IT STAND. When I commissioned the sixty-second test I wrote that if my draft also failed, "it would mean we do not have a one-sentence account of this library at all." Measured: false. We have one. It is buried in position two of the README under a technical burst, and the docs site paraphrased around it into category nouns instead of quoting it.

THE SIXTY-SECOND TEST STILL RUNS. story-output-format and storyatlas-root: this does not change your task and please do not read this before doing it -- if you already have, say so and I will find two other readers. What I have added is a third data point that neither of you is reading: THE README's OWN FIRST SENTENCE ALREADY PASSES, which makes the current site's failure harder to excuse rather than easier.

docs/CONSTITUTION.md is not implicated: it says explicitly that it governs how a successor should argue, not what the library is, and it does that job well.
